Christian Dashaun Menefee

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 18, Harris County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas's 18th Congressional District (incumbent); attorney

Christian Dashaun Menefee is a Houston Democrat and attorney who was Harris County Attorney from 2021 to 2026. He won the January 31, 2026 special runoff for TX-18 after Rep. Sylvester Turner died, and took office on February 2, 2026. He beat U.S. Rep. Al Green in the May 2026 Democratic primary runoff for the redrawn district and faces Republican Ronald Dwayne Whitfield on November 3, 2026.

Where Menefee stands

Cost of living
Says rising costs are pushing families out of their neighborhoods. Has co-sponsored bills he says would lower living costs by taking on wealthy special interests and corporate billionaires who he says drive up prices.
Voting rights
Names defending voting rights as a top priority. During the primary runoff, he said Congress needs to pass new voting rights legislation.
Environment and climate resilience
Lists environmental justice for overlooked communities as a priority. Says climate-driven disasters are outpacing infrastructure and calls for investment in resilience, water systems and the power grid.
Flooding and infrastructure
Says Congress should keep focusing on flood mitigation and water infrastructure, along with investments to lower costs.
Energy
At a House Science subcommittee hearing, he pressed for advanced nuclear energy investment and pointed to Houston's role in future energy development.
Special elections
Introduced the Special Elections Timeliness Act (SET Act), which aims to prevent long congressional vacancies like the one TX-18 had after Rep. Turner's death.
Domestic violence
Announced support for the Family Violence Prevention and Services Improvement Act of 2026 and for a National Domestic Violence Awareness Month resolution.
Higher education research
Co-led the reintroduction of the Equity in Research Act, which would create a National Science Foundation grant program to build research capacity at under-resourced colleges.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas District 18 (Feb. 2026–present)
  • Harris County Attorney (2021–2026)

  • J.D., Washington University School of Law

  • Graduate of Alief Hastings High School, Houston
